check.description: Two arms, and exactly one runs. SNAPSHOT: a positional population is checked against the model's constraints. TRANSITION: --pre, --steps and --post audit a WALK -- the operation invocations claimed to have carried the pre-population to the post-population -- reporting failed preconditions, undeclared side effects and illegal intermediate states. Mixing the two, or supplying part of the transition triple, is a usage error at 64: they answer different questions, and silently preferring one would make the other's arguments decorative. Model version 3 supports guarded Date plus/minus Duration calendar-day terms (date_add/date_sub), selecting report v11; --admission selects temporal report v13.

codegen.description: Turn model.orm.yaml into a plain-Python project with the GND shape: <package>/tools.py (one derived function per fact type, named and parameterized through the published model-id to Python-symbol mapping, with docstrings derived from the model's readings), the four-file extraction artifact bundle under artifacts/, a code-emitted SKILL.md the terminal agent runs, and create-once extension files (pyproject.toml, references/) that regeneration never rewrites. No provider SDK and no network library is emitted, so the generated project is CI-runnable with zero network and no API key — the agent running the generated SKILL.md is the only place a model is ever called. Every emitted Python module is parsed before any byte reaches disk. Re-running over an existing generated project is idempotent: an unchanged model performs ZERO writes and leaves every hash identical. A derived file you hand-edited, and an unmanaged file sitting at a derived path, are REFUSED rather than overwritten; --force overwrites them and still never touches an extension file. Exits 0 when the tree is written or already current, 3 when the model is invalid, two of its ids sanitize to one Python symbol (rename one), or the existing manifest is unreadable, 11 when a write was refused and nothing was destroyed, 64 on usage errors, 70 when an emitter invariant breaks over an already-valid model, 74 when the output path is refused or unwritable.

conformance.description: Ask whether a project `gnd codegen` generated still agrees with the model it came from. FOUR assertions run. Two are exact and corroborating: INTEGRITY — every code-emitted file still hashes to what the codegen manifest recorded — and CURRENCY, the manifest's model digest against the model's digest now, which IS model-code drift: the model moved and the code did not. Both are importable functions rather than CLI-only paths, so a downstream tool can invoke them without going through argv. The third is STRUCTURAL, and it is the assertion that makes a green result mean anything: the emitted surface is checked against the fact types the MODEL declares, computed from the model and the filesystem and never from the manifest or a previous generation. Without it the other two establish only that the generator agrees with itself — a project that is well-formed and empty, with every digest re-signed, passes both. The fourth is ARCHITECTURE: authored module, symbol, artifact and entry-point declarations are compared with static filesystem and AST observations without executing the project. Fully offline over committed artifacts, and the generated project is NEVER imported — this command reads bytes and hashes them, because importing a module to inspect it would execute the project's own code on every CI run. What a GREEN result does not say travels in the payload, not only in this text: every file the manifest records appears in either `examined` or `unexamined` by integrity, and extension files (pyproject.toml, references/) are not digest-gated because human- and LLM-authored text is not byte-reproducible and cannot be digest-gated, and the required `limits` block names the manifest co-edit blind spot — a manifest cannot record its own digest, so a derived file edited TOGETHER with its manifest entry is undetectable by digest comparison, exactly as in `gnd doctor`. Two runs over one unchanged project print byte-identical JSON. Exits 0 when all four assertions ran and found nothing, 13 when the generated code no longer matches its model (one band for the whole command — the payload names which assertion and which file), 3 when the codegen manifest will not parse, 64 on usage errors, 66 when the manifest or the model is missing so nothing could be compared at all (fail closed — a check that could not run must not read as one that passed), 74 when the project tree could not be read.

doccheck.description: Discharge the gnd-render-doc skill's obligations by CODE over the document manifest (skill prose explains, validators discharge). Four obligations: (1) binding — document_sha256, source_population_sha256 and applicable_sha256 match the actual file bytes; (2) rendering — every role filler of every APPLICABLE fact type in the source population is mentioned in the document under lexical normalization, direct fillers as their value and composite fillers via their identifying component values; inapplicable fact types are exempt BY the published applicable-set artifact, never by leniency; (3) distractors — at least one of each kind (out-of-model, near-miss-entity, absent-fact), every distractor text present in the document, and every absent-fact distractor genuinely absent from the source population; (4) renderer identity fields non-empty. close.description: Refuse to close an experiment that did not finish what it declared. The verdict is a difference of two SETS — the question ids in SPEC.md and the resolution ids in CONCLUSIONS.md — and it fails when EITHER difference is non-empty: a declared question left unresolved, or an orphan answer to a question nobody asked. It also fails when a resolution's evidence pointer does not name a file inside the experiment directory, or when a follows: reference names an experiment that does not exist or has not concluded. The OUTCOME VALUES never affect the verdict. An experiment whose every question honestly resolves to 'unanswered' with a reason and a citation CLOSES at exit 0 — a gate that demanded success would pay for lying, and the gate's job is that a question cannot be quietly forgotten, not that experiments succeed. This is a validator, not a state machine: nothing is written and no status is recorded. Exits 0 when every obligation is discharged, 3 when SPEC.md or CONCLUSIONS.md is unparseable, schema-invalid, or declares another experiment's id, 14 when an obligation is undischarged INCLUDING a missing CONCLUSIONS.md (the gate's own verdict — the experiment is open, not the input missing), 64 on usage errors, 66 when SPEC.md is missing entirely, 74 when the directory cannot be read.

fidelity.description: Measure the EXTRACTOR, per fact type, over committed case directories. This command emits RATES and never a per-run verdict — it is the dual of `gnd verify`, which emits verdicts and never a rate: a checker pass over an uncalibrated extraction is not evidence of faithfulness. Matching is by the model's own reference scheme under a LEXICAL-only normalization, multiset (tp per identity key is min(source_count, extracted_count)), with INCLUSIVE precision (unresolved and ambiguous extractions stay in the denominator) and `ambiguous` as an explicit outcome for normalization collisions and broken composite identities — never an arbitrary match. Every rate ships with its numerator AND denominator, no figure blends fact types, and the payload is schema-REQUIRED to report calibration.state 'uncalibrated' and publishable false: the round trip measures the round trip, and while the calibration set is deferred no interval field may exist at all. Fully offline over committed artifacts. Exits 0 with the report, 3 on a digest binding mismatch inside a case, 64 on usage errors or a case set spanning more than one model, 66 when a required extraction artifact is missing (fail closed — a missing applicable set must not read as coverage), 70 on an internal contract breach, 74 when the output path is refused.

review.description: Advisory multi-CLI review over ONE of exactly three input classes — a plan, an experiment outcome, or a spec/results/delta bundle. GND attempts six reviewer seats over five installed terminal-agent CLIs (claude, codex, qwen, gemini, kimi, plus a glm seat that runs the claude CLI against Z.AI's Anthropic-compatible endpoint) through fixed Python-owned invocation argv and bounded prompt transport (stdin for five, one --prompt argv element for Kimi), keeps one closed envelope per reviewer including every timeout, authentication failure, missing executable and unparseable response, and requires three DISTINCT schema-valid successes before any panel result may be reported. Every reviewer must first return substantive help that documents every long flag in the invocation GND is about to send; an incompatible reviewer is never invoked. GND does not sandbox reviewer CLIs or enforce read-only execution. It verifies the reviewed artifacts are unchanged before publishing a run. The panel ships no provider SDK and sources no credentials.
review.listed_help: run the bounded six-reviewer advisory panel and finalize its synthesis (REV-01)

finalize.description: Take one immutable panel RUN directory and one closed SYNTHESIS document — the semantic grouping an agent authored over the successful responses — and prove it before rendering: the synthesis must bind the run by digest, account for every retained concern exactly once, give every agreed concern at least two DISTINCT successful supporting reviewers, keep every evidence-backed singleton under divergent views, and trace every prioritized fix to the complete supporter and evidence set of each group it touches. Reviewer quorum (three) and concern agreement (two) are different thresholds and neither substitutes for the other. Nothing in a reviewed artifact is ever written, no fix is applied, and an existing report is never replaced. Exits 0 when the report is rendered, 16 when the run itself is below quorum, 3 when the run evidence or the synthesis fails closed validation, 11 when the report path already exists, 64 on usage errors, 66 when the run directory or the synthesis is missing, 74 on refused or failed path/IO.
finalize.listed_help: validate a semantic synthesis against immutable run evidence and render it

panel.description: Load and digest-bind a review request, attempt all six reviewers concurrently under one shared deadline, and publish the normalized request, four raw streams and one closed envelope per reviewer, every validated response, and a manifest-last run.json into a directory that must not already exist. REQUEST and every artifact it names are repository-relative paths resolved against the directory you are standing in. Every bound must be strictly positive and is validated BEFORE any process is spawned; each reviewer's deadline is the earlier of --reviewer-timeout and the remaining --overall-timeout. Prints one closed JSON summary and never a verdict, a rate, or a conformance result. Exits 0 when at least three distinct reviewers returned schema-valid responses, 16 when all six attempts completed and fewer than three did, 3 when the request or a reviewer-cited artifact is ill-formed, 11 when the output directory already exists (nothing was written and no reviewer was invoked), 64 on usage errors including a non-positive bound, 66 when the request or a reviewed artifact is missing, 70 on an internal defect, 74 on refused or failed path/IO.

solve.description:
Walk the CLI-pure GND stations in locked order -- validate, synth, codegen, exp-run, conformance -- blocking for an authorization before each one and appending an authorization record to a walk log before the station is spawned.

WHAT THIS GUARANTEES: sequence, gating and logging FOR WALKS THAT GO THROUGH IT. Nothing more.

WHAT IT DOES NOT GUARANTEE: the process in general. Running the stations a la carte stays legal and is not a violation of anything -- a harness that could not be bypassed would be routed around, and a bypassed harness is worse than none, because its log's existence would falsely imply the walk is where work happens.

IT DOES NOT JUDGE STATION-INTERNAL AGENT WORK. The guarantee's perimeter is the walk log's perimeter.

A STATION'S OWN EXIT IS IN THE LOG, NOT IN THIS COMMAND'S EXIT CODE. The exit code is a control plane: 0 a completed walk or informational action, 17 a walk that halted at a station, 64 usage, 66 a missing path, 70 an internal defect, 74 an I/O refusal. A caller scripting this command reads the code and then reads the log; a station exiting 11 does not make gnd solve claim a collision about itself.

THE BROWNFIELD PROFILE ASSUMES RECOVERY ALREADY COMPLETED. --skip synth --skip codegen --skip conformance leaves gnd validate; a recovered model's gate is gnd recovery verify, which runs BEFORE this harness is entered, not inside it.

THE WALK LOG RECORDS WHAT THIS HARNESS DID; IT IS NOT PROOF THAT IT DID IT. A log that satisfies the walk predicate is a self-consistent document, and a file authored by hand can be self-consistent too. It attests no spawn, no executed argv, no existing artifact and no human presence.

THE OUTER STATION TIMEOUT IS NOT THE CONTRACT'S INNER --wall-seconds BOUND. --station-timeout bounds the child process; this harness passes no --wall-seconds to gnd exp run, because a contract's own wall bound is the contract's business.
solve.listed_help: walk the CLI-pure GND stations in order, gating each, and log the walk

synth.description: Generate labelled synthetic populations, each with a provenance SIDECAR. --class conforming builds populations the checker accepts; --class violating mutates a conforming baseline, one population per (constraint, operator) pair, each admitted only after the real checker confirms the model-derived typed prediction (D-05'); --class all does both. The development lane is probabilistic by default: --seed omitted draws OS entropy per population and records it, so data is fresh yet regenerable; --seed N is the deterministic variant-regeneration path. --pool consumes an admitted pool artifact; an omitted --pool builds and materialises a Faker pool beside the corpus. Exits 5 on a generator invariant failure, 6 on a quarantined checker/witness or prediction/observation disagreement (C1).

uninstall.description: Remove every skill file GND placed at the requested target roots. A file is deleted only when its bytes still hash to what the install receipt recorded, so anything you edited is KEPT and named in the report — there is deliberately no flag that overrides this. Files GND never placed are never touched. The directories emptied by the removal are pruned and the receipt is removed last. Unlike `doctor`, this acts on exactly the scope you name. Exits 0 on a clean removal, 10 when something was kept, 12 when nothing is installed, 74 when a receipt could not be trusted (in which case nothing at all was deleted). Text output only (D-25).

verify.description: Run the full derived verifier: popvalidate then check over a PRE-EXTRACTED population file. This command never calls a model and never orchestrates extraction (R-03''): the executing agent running the gnd-extract skill writes the population and its <population>.extraction.json sidecar, and verify validates the handoff before composing the checker. Exit bands are REUSED unchanged with precedence 3 > 1 > 4 > 2 > 0: 3 ill-formed (including an ill-formed extraction handoff), 1 alethic fail, 4 indeterminate, 2 vacuous, 0 pass. The payload's extraction block carries the machine-readable state (ran | skipped | failed + reason); a missing sidecar is extraction:sidecar-missing, a malformed one extraction:sidecar-invalid, and a digest that does not match the file bytes extraction:binding-mismatch — all exit 3, state failed. skipped is written ONLY by --no-extraction. Never a fidelity rate in this payload: a checker pass over an uncalibrated extraction is checker acceptance, not proof of faithfulness.
